questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding pouring of molten metal in mould cavity?

options.text: The temperature at which pouring is done is around 20% more than the melting temperature of the metal.
Higher the pouring temperature, higher is the fluidity of the metal.
If the pouring rate is too slow, the tendency of formation of metal oxides is more which can get entrapped during solidification.
If the pouring rate is too high, turbulence can occur in molten metal flow.

questions.solution:
(c)
If the pouring rate is too slow, the metal will chill and freeze before filling the cavity. The formation of metal oxides is accelerated by turbulence in fluid motion which occurs when the pouring rate is too high.

questions.qtext: Which of the following is not an advantage of powder metallurgy processing?

options.text: Such processing involves little wastage of raw material.
Such processing produces near net shape products.
The raw material being in powdered form is easy to store and handle.
Difficult to fabricate materials like tungsten can be readily shaped using such processing method.

questions.solution:
(c)
One of the major difficulties in PM processing is with storing and handling of metal powders. This is because metal powders are generally highly reactive and prone to degradation over time and fire hazards with particular metals.

questions.qtext: Which of the following are correct settings of power source in resistance welding?

options.text: Low current; High voltage; Short duration
High current; Low voltage; Short duration
High current; Low voltage; Long duration
High current; High voltage; Short duration

questions.solution:
(b)
The current used in resistance welding operations is very high (5000 to 20000A), although voltage is relatively low (usually below 10V). The duration of current is short, lasting 0.1 to 0.4s in most processes.
